rootCause.subtitle: Business processes are hardcoded to job titles — not business functions.
rootCause.label: Position-Based Process Design
rootCause.description: Business processes are hardcoded to job titles (positions) instead of business functions. When positions change, processes break.
rootCause.depDesc: Every process is tied to a specific job title. If the title changes, the process flow must be redesigned.
rootCause.depExample: "Head of Procurement" is removed → 12 related SOPs become invalid
rootCause.docDesc: Every position change triggers massive revisions to SOPs, work instructions, and related forms.
rootCause.docExample: 1 directorate restructuring → 847 pages of documents must be revised
rootCause.handoffDesc: Because processes are designed based on positions, excessive hand-offs occur between positions.
rootCause.handoffExample: Average 8.2 hand-offs per process, ideal is < 5
rootCause.cycleDesc: Position-bound processes have longer cycle times because approval chains follow hierarchy, not function.
rootCause.cycleExample: 6-level approval chain → 14-day cycle time (should be 5 days)
rootCause.conclusionText: All four issues stem from one thing: processes are designed based on job positions, not business functions. The solution is Function-Based BPMN — decoupling process architecture from organizational structure.
